author: Grok, independent read of the attempt-002 exit-reason payload and the pinned desktop XNU tree
compared_with: reports/sprint-010/shared-shell-return-attempt002-sigkill-exit-reason-analysis.json is the author analysis. This receipt does not adopt it.
source_limit: This is the pinned desktop tree. It is not a disassembly of kernelcache 02fe2d4106ca3091b95a3e9235e3f9a7226c0f030eb24fb609f6817506c0f883.

kcdata: PID type 0x36 size 16 flags 0x8c logical 4 bytes, int32 value 14
PROCNAME type 0x37 size 48 flags 0x8f logical 33 bytes, C string chonk-terminal-darwin, following nonzero bytes 6f70

what_matches_pinned_xnu: kill() calls psignal with no reason (kern_sig.c kill). psignal calls psignal_internal with a NULL reason. For SIGKILL, if the target thread's uu_exit_reason is still null and no reason was passed, psignal_internal calls build_signal_reason(signum, NULL) and set_thread_exit_reason.

build_signal_reason(signum, NULL) sets namespace OS_REASON_SIGNAL and code to the signal number. The PID item is proc_getpid(current_proc()). The PROCNAME item is requested at sizeof(p_name), which is proc_name_t, 2*MAXCOMLEN+1 = 33, and the NULL-procname branch copies the whole p_name. An explicit procname is copied with strlen only into a zeroed buffer.

The 128-byte payload matches that layout: OS reason begin, one PID 14, one 33-byte name whose C string is chonk-terminal-darwin, and two nonzero bytes after the NUL. Those tail bytes match a whole-p_name copy. They do not match a strlen copy of an explicit name.

The sender recorded in the payload is therefore the process that was current when build_signal_reason ran. That process is pid 14, the reaped application. A kill syscall whose current process was the desktop (console DL23_DESKTOP_PID pid=13) would record pid 13. The attempt 0 journal has TermAttempt and KillAttempt absent.
where_the_author_analysis_does_not_match: cs_invalid_page calls threadsignal(current_thread(), SIGKILL, EXC_BAD_ACCESS, FALSE) only when CS_KILL is set (kern_cs.c). threadsignal builds a reason only when set_exitreason is true, and the name it passes is the literal exc handler. The CS_KILL call does not build that reason.

vm_fault_enter, when cs_killed is true, creates OS_REASON_CODESIGNING with code CODESIGNING_EXIT_REASON_INVALID_PAGE (2) and set_thread_exit_reason installs it only while uu_exit_reason is still null (vm_fault.c). The captured namespace is OS_REASON_SIGNAL and the code is 9. The CS_KILL page path in this tree installs a codesigning reason, so it is not the path that installed this record. CS_EXEC_SET_KILL in kern_exec.c ORs CS_KILL into the image flags; if that later took the page-kill path, the installed reason would still be the codesigning reason.

The console has two cs_invalid_page lines, both the non-kill text allowing (remove VALID): pid 1 launchd and pid 2 launchctl, final status 0x20020000. Neither line is pid 14. A silent CS_KILL or already-invalid call would not print when cs_debug is 0, so the missing line is not itself proof. The namespace in the exit reason is the contradicting fact.

kern_memorystatus.c calls psignal(p, SIGKILL) with no jetsam reason at three sites. Those calls also go through build_signal_reason(NULL) and record current_proc, so a jetsam namespace is not what those sites write. They match this payload only when current_proc at the call is pid 14. This receipt does not show that those sites ran.
The CodeDirectory flag value 0x20002 was not re-parsed from the application binary here.
paths_that_do_not_produce_this_payload: process_signature failure uses psignal_vfork_with_reason with an EXEC, CODESIGNING, or SECURITY reason (kern_exec.c). That reason's namespace is not OS_REASON_SIGNAL. Spawn for pid 14 returned 0 at stage 10 before the reap.

The default vnguard flags in kern_guarded.c are LOGMSG, EXC_CORPSE, and UPRINTMSG. kVNG_POLICY_SIGKILL is a separate bit and is not in that default. The saved guest original-bootargs.bin contains no vnguard text. The SIGKILL policy branch would be psignal(current_proc(), SIGKILL), which would match this shape only if that branch ran on pid 14.

CS_OPS_MARKINVALID and CS_OPS_MARKKILL in kern_proc.c call psignal(target, SIGKILL) with no reason, so the recorded sender is the caller. A caller other than pid 14 would record that caller's pid. No CS_OPS_MARKKILL or CS_OPS_MARKINVALID call site was found under integrations/puredarwin.
attempt_1: Attempt 1, pid 15, was reaped with application wait 0. Its exit_reason line is query_failed errno=2. Pinned proc_pidinfo returns ENOENT when the kernel has no exit reason. That is a recorded query result for a different process. It does not identify the signal that killed pid 14.
conclusion: The captured reason was built as OS_REASON_SIGNAL code 9 while current_proc was pid 14 and that process's p_name began with chonk-terminal-darwin. The pinned sources make that the sender identity for a NULL-reason SIGKILL path. They do not identify which of those call sites ran. The CS_KILL page path described in the author analysis does not install this namespace or this procname in this tree. The subsystem that raised the SIGKILL is not established.
not_claimed: the exact kernel subsystem that raised the SIGKILL
